featured_reviews.review_text:
We had the chance to visit Udupi to Mumbai restaurant in BKC on their inaugural day, and it was a wonderful experience. The restaurant beautifully brings together South Indian cuisine and Maharashtrian food with pure authenticity, which makes the menu very unique and exciting.

The food tasted amazing and truly reflected authentic flavors from both regions. As it was their opening day, the food was served complimentary, which was such a thoughtful gesture and made the customers feel really overwhelmed and welcomed.

Overall, it was a lovely experience and I would definitely recommend visiting this place if you want to enjoy authentic South Indian and maharashtra food.. their thattu idly,penne masala dosa and misel pav must must try

featured_reviews.name: Greville Kharlukhi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Its simply just convenient. Nothing memorable

Cos of the veg array

I keep coming back to this vegetarian restaurant, and if I’m being honest, geography is doing a lot of the heavy lifting here. It’s conveniently close enough that my laziness can overpower my cravings for a while.

The food is fresh, well-made, and clearly prepared with care. The menu does a commendable job of convincing vegetables to impersonate things they were never meant to be. Some dishes even come dangerously close to making me forget about real food- meat.

Unfortunately, I was raised on a steady diet of creatures that once had opinions, so my deeply ingrained bias toward real food remains the ultimate buzzkill. Every bite is accompanied by a tiny voice in my head asking, “This is nice, but we paying
Fr veggie food bro?”

That said, if you’re vegetarian, you’ll probably love it. If you’re a carnivore like me, you’ll still enjoy it—especially if it’s close enough that convenience can temporarily defeat instinct.

Would return. Mostly because it’s nearby. Partly. Thats it

On the forefront of this love story is Chef Amninder Sandhu, a bawri who has set out to rekindle the romance of traditional Indian cooking through a menu that pays homage to age old recipes, and techniques that are almost long-lost, and bold, complex flavours. Allow yourself to walk down memory lane as we trigger childhood memories through our food, whilst you eat with your hands and return to tradition. featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Bawri for lunch, and the experience was truly amazing. The restaurant has beautiful, aesthetic interiors with a warm and elegant vibe that makes it perfect for a relaxed dining experience.

We started with Mutton Kakori Kebab and Chicken Smoked Tikka, both perfectly cooked and packed with rich flavors. Alongside, the Hibiscus Cranberry Lemonade and Kaji Lemon Ice Tea were refreshing and well-balanced.

For mains, the Bawri Butter Chicken with Bawri Naan was creamy and indulgent, while the Mutton Biryani stood out with its aromatic spices and tender meat.

We ended on a high note with the Masala Chai Cheesecake, which was a unique and delightful dessert. Overall, a wonderful lunch experience with great food, ambience, and service.

featured_reviews.name: falguni doshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bawri was our family lunch place last week and it was a pleasant experience, the interiors are good and the staff took good care of us. These dishes are what we liked the most - you can definitely try them.

Dhakai Chaat, Ghugni and Gutti Aloo - we wanted to try something unique and they suggested this lesser known chaat from East India. The Gutti Aloo in the center was really tasty while the ghugni was creamy and comforting.

Dal Makhani with Bawri Naan - A must try from my side, the dal makhani was really top notch! The flavours were unlocked via slow cooking and it was really rich. The Bawri naan as suggested by the staff paired really well and gave it a nice garlicky spicy touch. Very good pairing and 100% recommend

Bawri Jamun - We ended with this dessert as we love gulab jamun and this was just superb! I especially loved the crunchy white chocolate at the bottom and this is really heavy - so leave some space for it. My husband and daughter loved the rabdi and we packed some more for them.

Very good place for family plans, if you like Indian food - you can definitely visit 💯

featured_reviews.name: Kaira Goradia
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to Bawri with my sisters for dinner and it was honestly such a good time. Everything we ate was incredible!

We started off with the Mango Bite and Coco Berry drinks; both were super refreshing. For the starters, the Thecha Potatoes were probably the best I’ve ever had, and the Chargrilled Broccoli was so tasty I’d go back just for that.

For the main part of the meal, the Paneer Kofta was so soft it basically melted in my mouth, especially with the Garlic and Lal Mirch Naan. We finished with Jalebi and Rabdi, which they made perfectly. Every single bite was heavenly.

Recently visited this new and beautiful looking place in BKC with a group of 8 people. We were a big group and wanted to spend some good quality time chatting over good food so we chose this new outlet called Dakshin Legacy.
Ambience: Just like the name suggests, indoors and ambience truly honour legacy of our colourful south India. Indoors are bright, lively, colourful with beautiful paintings and artefacts around. There’s even a life-size statue of Bharatanatyam dancer to pose with. So much said about the beauty of this place, if only I would’ve had anything to speak about food.
Food: Extremely under thought and blundered menu with same dishes lining up in 2-3 different sections. We ordered nearly quarter of their dishes and to be honest nothing pleased our palates. The vegetarian options like stuffed mushroom, tandoori starter platter, veg crispy were still good, but non veg options were spiced to death in form of raw chilli. Value for money: Ambience was good, you can come here for some worthy pictures but if you get out for food, this is not the place you should be at. Can easily be missed out on, unless you want colourful serenity.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Follow me for more content on Instagram @kapaianita

A promising new addition to Bandra Kurla Complex, this newly opened restaurant delivers a comforting, well-rounded dining experience backed by warm, attentive hospitality.

The clear highlights of the meal were the Pomfret Hariyali and the Matka Chicken Tandoori. The pomfret was fresh, delicately cooked, and coated in a vibrant green marinade that enhanced rather than masked the flavour of the fish. The matka chicken arrived beautifully tender, smoky, and aromatic—easily a must-order for tandoor lovers.

The Prawns Pullimanchi impressed with its robust, punchy flavours and paired exceptionally well with the Neer Dosa, whose soft, subtle texture balanced the intensity of the dish perfectly.

Starters like the Paneer Cheese Kebab and Harabhara Kebab were well-seasoned and comforting. For mains, the Paneer Butter Masala was rich yet balanced, best enjoyed with Cheese Garlic Naan or flaky Malabar Parota, while the slow-cooked Dal Makhani offered familiar, homely comfort. Crisp Papad rounded off the savoury courses.

The bar added to the experience with a smooth Espresso Martini and the innovative “Lungi Dance” cocktail, playful yet well-crafted.

Desserts kept things classic and indulgent with Gajar Halva, Gulab Jamun with Ice Cream, and a nostalgic Oreo Milkshake.

Polite, efficient service led by Keval made the experience feel relaxed and welcoming. A strong start for this new BKC address, with standout tandoor and seafood dishes that deserve attention.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries in Bandra has such a gorgeous, welcoming vibe, it’s easily one of the prettiest spots for South Indian food in the city. The staff was genuinely sweet and the service was so smooth it made the whole experience feel really relaxed.

We decided to try their new chaat menu, and the Shakkarkand Matar ki Chaat was a total winner, it felt super fresh and not at all oily. The Chatpata Singhada (water chestnut) was a fun surprise too, especially for that unique crunch you don't usually find in street food.

The Madras Diaries Special Combo is a solid choice if you’re like me and can't decide the medu vada was perfectly crispy. But honestly, the real highlight was the Filter Coffee with those Rawa Biscuits. It’s such a nostalgic, comforting pairing. We finished with the Elaneer Payasum, which was light and refreshing, though I wish there was just a bit more of it! Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Bandra and want a meal that feels both clean and satisfying.

The Chatpata Singhada and Shakkarkand Matar Ki Chaat were vibrant, tangy, and full of flavour. The Chettinad Paneer with flaky wheat parotta was rich and satisfying, paired beautifully with the soft Kodumai (wheat) parotta. Refreshing sips like the Cold Coffee and Virgin Mojito balanced the meal, while the Elaneer Payasam was a light, delicious finish.

The presentation of each dish was impressive and clearly made with attention to detail. Service was warm and prompt, making the overall experience even more enjoyable.

With its warm décor and relaxed, inviting ambience, Madras Diaries is a must-visit for a wholesome meal with a unique chaat twist!

featured_reviews.review_text:
A completely disgusting experience on 31st December. Me and my group of friends had paid around 18k at the time of booking itself. We had to wait outside for a while since they were having an argument with some other customers. Then upon entering, they said we will not be able to provide you a table, so we'll have to stand at the bar. However all the tables in the restaurant were empty, they had forced everyone there to stand at the bar, saying the tables can't be given to us unless we pay an additional 5k per head. After a lot of argument they finally relented and gave us a table with 4 seats when we were a group of 7, but only until 11:00, after which they would start charging us the 5k.
We ordered some starters and within 2 mins the waiter arrived with the bill, saying he will keep bringing the bill after every order since it's very busy, so we will have to settle up everytime right then and there, including the service charge which they had very conveniently made mandatory for the night.
When we had entered, they had given us multiple coupons of 1k each, totaling 18k, to use to settle up the tab. At one point, when the bill had reached 13098, we paid them 13k in coupons and asked them to carry forward the 98 for the next bill. The waiter however kept demanding that we should give him 1 more coupon of 1000, which also he would not adjust in the next bill. So basically he wanted us to pay 1000 for a mere additional 98. All of this "chhindigiri" is happening when we have already paid 18k, so either way the restaurant was as it is in a profit of 5k.
This level of cheapness is the last thing any of us expected from a restaurant that claims to be so posh and high class. The waiter and manager were very rude, we had to physically go to the kitchen to ask for water multiple times since they refused to actually pay attention to the order we were asking them to bring.
Horrible service from a place that charges exorbitant rates from people in exchange for a pleasant experience.
I understand the concept of supply and demand, but they are simply taking advantage of people, especially on a popular night and robbing their customers blind.
Never will any of my family, friends, or their family and friends ever go to this disgusting establishment again.

featured_reviews.name: Kapil Jaiswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Last evening, visited O Pedro at Godrej BKC to catch up with friends, and overall it turned out to be a lively and enjoyable experience. The restaurant definitely has a strong personality of its own — vibrant ambience, energetic crowd, good music, and a stylish Goan-Latin inspired vibe that makes it feel different from the usual BKC dining places.

The ambience and overall vibe are honestly one of the biggest strengths of O Pedro. The place feels warm, colourful, and social without becoming too loud or chaotic. It’s ideal for group outings and long conversations over food and drinks. The interiors are beautifully done, and the energy of the place keeps the atmosphere upbeat throughout the evening.

Coming to the food and drinks, we ordered quite a variety.

The Stranger & Sons cocktail was refreshing and smooth with balanced botanical flavours. It paired really well with the starters.

The Crab Ros Omelette was flavourful and rich, with soft eggs wrapped around well-seasoned crab filling. It had a comforting yet indulgent taste.

The Malaki Indian Tonic was light, crisp, and refreshing, making it a good accompaniment during the meal.

The Guava Pineapple Sour had a tropical sweetness balanced nicely with a sour finish. Refreshing and enjoyable without being overly sweet.

The Choriz Chilly Fry (Gluten Free) was one of the highlights. Packed with bold Goan flavours, smoky spice, and excellent texture, it paired wonderfully with drinks.

The Grilled Chicken Peri Peri was juicy and well-marinated with balanced heat levels. The chicken was cooked properly without drying out.

The Picante Highballin cocktail had a nice spicy-citrus profile and worked very well for those who enjoy slightly stronger flavours.

The All Poee Basket and freshly served Poee were excellent accompaniments. Soft, fresh, and authentic, they complemented the spicy dishes beautifully.

The Cardoz’s Chicken Chilli Fry had strong coastal flavours with a nice spice kick. The preparation felt rustic and flavourful.

The Monkey Shoulder (60ml) was smooth and enjoyable as expected for whisky lovers.

The Roasted Lamb Chops were tender, juicy, and cooked well. The seasoning was balanced and allowed the flavour of the meat to stand out nicely.

We ended with Aunty Li’s Serradura, which was creamy, light, and a perfect dessert to finish the meal without feeling too heavy.

The staff throughout the evening was courteous, attentive, and helpful. Service was fairly smooth despite the restaurant being busy.

However, there were a few things that slightly impacted the overall experience.

The first was the extremely high cover charge for confirmed bookings. Charging ₹1,000 per person through food apps for securing a preferred time slot felt excessive, even though the amount gets adjusted in the final bill. Most restaurants usually charge somewhere between ₹50–₹250 for reservation commitments, so ₹1,000 per head honestly feels unnecessarily high.

Secondly, while the food quality was good, some dishes did feel slightly overpriced and somewhat overhyped considering the portion sizes and overall value.

Another small drawback was that towards the later part of the evening, there seemed to be subtle pressure to vacate the table for the next guests. While understandable from an operational perspective, it could definitely have been handled in a more polished and guest-friendly manner, especially when people are dining and catching up socially.

That said, the overall experience was still enjoyable because of the good vibes, lively ambience, flavourful food, and pleasant company. O Pedro is definitely a place worth visiting at least once for its atmosphere and unique menu.

Overall, a good experience with some room for improvement in guest handling and pricing balance. Great for catching up with friends and enjoying a vibrant evening in BKC.

featured_reviews.name: Shreyas Saddalgi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Malgudi: Great Vibes, Confused Kitchen & Extra Fees
Let’s be real—I wanted to love this place. Walking into Malgudi on SV Road, the vibe is immaculate. It sets you up for a cozy, authentic South Indian experience. But between the kitchen confusion and the final bill, it’s a bit of a rollercoaster.
Here is the unfiltered breakdown:
The Star of the Show
If you go here, do yourself a favor and order the Benne Masala Dosa. It was genuinely too good—crispy, buttery, and exactly what you hope for. The chutney pairing was also on point and very tasty.
The "What happened here?" Section
Unfortunately, the rest of the meal felt like an identity crisis.
• The Sambar Situation: This was weird. The sambar actually tasted different across different dishes. Consistency is key, guys—pick a lane!
• Portions & Options: The menu feels very limited, and the portion sizes are basically a tease. For the price, you expect to leave full, not looking for a snack on the way home.
• Overall Taste: Aside from the Benne Dosa, the general taste could really be improved. It feels like they are holding back flavor.
The Coffee Letdown
For a place with this vibe, you expect the coffee game to be strong. It wasn't.
• Coffee Mocktails: Hard pass. They just felt not worth the price tag.
• Filter Coffee: The ultimate test for a South Indian spot, and they failed it. It tasted average at best and definitely lacked that authentic "kick" you crave.
The Final Pinch
Just when you are questioning the portion sizes vs. the price, the bill arrives. They levy a 5% Service Charge.
Paying extra for "service" when the filter coffee is average and the sambar is inconsistent? That stings.
The Verdict
Go for the Benne Masala Dosa and the aesthetic, but lower your expectations for everything else. It’s a great place to sit, but be ready to pay a premium (plus 5%) for a mixed bag of flavors.

featured_reviews.name: Ankeeta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Thuppa Dosa House is a cozy, warm haven for lovers of South Indian food. As soon as you step in, there's a friendly hustle in the air — the staff are welcoming, attentive, and genuinely seem happy to guide you through the menu. The décor, though modest, is tastefully done: soft lighting, comfortable seating, and enough of an open kitchen vibe to let you see your dosa being made, which adds to the experience.

The signature dishes are the stars. The Benne Podi Masala Dosa is a must-try: buttery, with the earthy bite of podi, it delivers both comfort and punch. Their Open Butter Masala Dosa is similarly divine — crisp edges, rich butter flavour, and generous servings that make you feel you’ve gotten your dosa’s worth. If you want something more delicate, try their Leaf Idli or Ghee Leaf Idli — soft, fragrant, with hints of ghee that elevate the simple idli into something special. People also rave about their Crispy Ghee Idli Vada. And of course, the classic Benne Dosa — probably their signature — thin, crisp, buttery edges, with that beautiful contrast of texture that leaves you wanting more.

Service is good; your order comes in a reasonable time, and the staff seem well-trained—they explain dishes if asked, bring out condiments and chutneys properly, and appear to care about the overall presentation. The ambience helps a lot: somewhat casual, not pretentious, but clean and pleasant — a perfect spot for breakfast, for a relaxed lunch, or even an informal dinner.

If you love dosa, you’ll especially love their Benne Dosa. It’s arguably the best there — buttery, crisp in all the right places, rich flavour without being greasy. Pair it with filter coffee or some of their fresh chutneys, and it’s almost perfect. Thuppa Dosa House hits that sweet spot between authenticity and comfort — hearty flavours, good service, and a space that makes you feel welcome.

featured_reviews.name: Raj Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Super Mani Restaurant is one of those rare places that gets the basics absolutely right, and that’s what makes it stand out. If you’re someone who appreciates simple South Indian food done well, this spot is worth your time. Their idlis, in particular, are easily among the best you’ll find anywhere.

What makes their idlis special is the texture. They are incredibly soft, light, and fluffy, almost melting the moment you take a bite. It’s clear that a lot of care goes into the batter and the fermentation process. They’re served fresh and steaming hot, which only adds to the experience. Pair that with their coconut chutney and sambar, and you’ve got a combination that feels comforting and satisfying without being heavy.

The chutneys are fresh and well-balanced, not overly spicy or bland, and the sambar has a rich, homely flavor that complements the idlis perfectly. Even during busy hours, the quality remains consistent, which says a lot about their kitchen standards.

The overall atmosphere is simple and no-frills, but clean and welcoming. Service is quick, and the staff keep things moving efficiently without making you feel rushed.

If you’re craving authentic South Indian breakfast or just a plate of really good idlis, Super Mani Restaurant delivers every single time. It’s the kind of place you’ll find yourself coming back to regularly, especially once you’ve tasted those idlis.
